provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: cue or word lost at the edge of the aligned window (target beata n, the 1862 layer be ta x); recogniser damage, same word: target reads exstitit, the 1862 layer reads xtitit; recogniser damage, same word: target reads merito castitatis, the 1862 layer reads m rito castit tis; recogniser damage, same word: target reads professione, the 1862 layer reads professi ne; conclusion length: the 1862 prints the short printed cue where the 1962 writes the conclusion out. Corroboration: 1922 Mame, artifact PDF p. 914 (printed p. 36* of the Commune Sanctorum); read from the page's word bounding boxes, reflowed column by column; reading: NDULGENTIAM nobis, que&- Domine, beata Bsns N. Virgo et Martyr imploret: que tibi grata. semper éxstitit, et mérito castitatis, et tuze professiéne virtitis. Per Dominum. Recorded limitation: Option set: this element belongs to the 'singular' set among this Common's mutually exclusive oration sets, and is proposed under that set alone; the sets are not merged. Target reading settled on the CMAA facsimile page image at 450 dpi; the crops read are kept in .scratch/backfill/commons-2/work/img.
